Where it began

Parthiv Patel was born in Ahmedabad on 9 March 1985. He batted left-handed, kept wicket and played his domestic cricket for Gujarat, and he reached the top of the game remarkably young.

The player

His Test debut came against England at Trent Bridge in 2002, when he was 17 years and 153 days old. That made him the youngest wicketkeeper Test cricket had seen, taking the record from Pakistan's Hanif Mohammed, who had been 17 years and 300 days. It was a debut with some grit in it, too. In the second innings he batted for 82 minutes to finish unbeaten on 19, with Zaheer Khan for company, and the match was drawn.

His Test career came in two chapters. Recalled at Mohali in November 2016, eight years after his previous Test, he made an unbeaten 67 from 54 balls in the second innings to help India to victory. In all he played 25 Tests between 2002 and 2018, scoring 934 runs at 31.13 with six fifties and a best of 71, and took 62 catches and 10 stumpings.

What made him special

His finest days as a leader came with Gujarat in the Ranji Trophy of 2016–17. As captain he took them to only their second final, against Mumbai, the holders, at Indore. He made 90 in the first innings and 143 in the second, the biggest score in a winning chase in a Ranji final, and Gujarat lifted the trophy for the first time. With that they became the first side, and he the first captain, to win all three of India's major domestic titles.

A Test hundred never quite came his way, though a best of 71 shows it was never far off.

Away from the middle

He was a busy IPL cricketer. In the first season he opened the batting with Matthew Hayden for Chennai Super Kings, he led Kochi Tuskers Kerala in 2011, and he later played for Mumbai Indians and Royal Challengers Bangalore. He was also part of the India squad that won the 2016 Asia Cup.

He retired from all cricket in December 2020 and moved straight into the game's other jobs: talent scout for Mumbai Indians, commentator on the IPL and on international matches, and from November 2024 assistant and batting coach of Gujarat Titans.

And finally

Between one Test and the next he waited eight years, while India played 83 Tests without him. He came back and helped win the match, which is about the best reply to a long wait that anyone could give.
